title: Inside the Thermostat
story:
Tomasz: The cold-room thermostat reads setpoint 25. It must be 18. Core samples cannot sit above 20.

You: Can I restart the container with new settings?

Tomasz: No. It has been recording since this morning, and its calibration log lives in the container's own temp files. A restart-and-recreate would erase the day's curve. Change the value inside the running container. The file is `/etc/thermostat/thermostat.conf` in the container `thermostat`; `setpoint=25` has to become `setpoint=18`.
objectives: Change `setpoint=25` to `setpoint=18` in `/etc/thermostat/thermostat.conf` inside the container `thermostat`
Keep the same container running: do not remove or recreate it
startingState: A container named `thermostat` is running with `setpoint=25` in its config and a calibration log at `/tmp/calibration.log`.
hints: You can run an extra command inside a container that is already running without touching its main process. That command family is `docker exec`.
The shape is `docker exec <container> <command>`. A one-line `sed -i 's/old/new/' file` edits a file without opening an editor; `cat` lets you verify the result.

```bash
docker exec thermostat cat /etc/thermostat/thermostat.conf
docker exec thermostat sed -i 's/setpoint=25/setpoint=18/' /etc/thermostat/thermostat.conf
docker exec thermostat cat /etc/thermostat/thermostat.conf
```

commands: docker run -d --name thermostat alpine:3.20 sh -c 'mkdir -p /etc/thermostat; echo setpoint=25 > /etc/thermostat/thermostat.conf; echo "day curve: 22 23 25" > /tmp/calibration.log; sleep infinity'

validation.description: The original container survived: `/tmp/calibration.log` still exists

debrief: `docker exec` starts a second process inside the same container, so it can inspect or repair a live service. Pro tip: changes made this way vanish if the container is recreated, so also fix the source of the config afterwards.
